document_title: VB CDC ROADM — Alarm and Troubleshooting Reference, Document VB-ROADM-ATR, issue 2

datasheet.value: An optical channel monitor on each ingress degree

monitors.name: optical channel monitor
monitors.availability: available on nodes with the channel monitoring option

when: An impairment affecting the whole incoming line
result: continues, after the node, as an impairment of each channel routed onwards

when: A power loss upstream of up to about 8 dB
result: does not appear downstream as low power
the loss of signal-to-noise ratio it caused remains
behaviours.note: equalises the channel powers to the launch target within its attenuation range, typically 8 dB

faults.name: WSS attenuation drift
faults.description: The WSS attenuation for one channel drifts above its set value.

faults.name: WSS passband shift
faults.description: The WSS passband for one channel is shifted or narrowed.

faults.name: WSS input port failure
applies_to: An input port of a WSS
faults.description: An input port of a WSS fails.

effects.scope: Every channel arriving at the node on that degree
channels arriving on the other degrees

routing: Each channel leaving a degree is switched separately.
troubleshooting_notes: The ROADM raises no alarms of its own for the faults below. They show in the channel monitor's readings and in the alarms of the line interfaces downstream.
A deviation in a channel's power at the channel monitors locates a single-channel fault at the node where the deviation first appears.
A port fault lies at the input port of the degree it affects.
A single-channel fault lies on that channel at the input port of the degree where it first appears.
